speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision; can you describe exactly how your leg was positioned when the accident happened and how you were moved?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Femoral Neck Fracture. The mechanism of injury (rear-end collision with the right rear axle striking the driver's right side) combined with immediate onset of right groin pain and inability to move the leg suggests an unstable fracture, likely a pertrochanteric or femoral neck fracture, which often presents with the leg held in external rotation.
